title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health data exposure, Nov 2026
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Microsoft, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: A worldwide cloud service, but Microsoft has not said how many organizations were affected, so this size is a provisional estimate. More than a dozen administrators reported getting the notice, per one outlet's description of a social media thread.
who_is_affected: Organizations that received Microsoft's notice through Azure Service Health, per Microsoft. It says they need no software update, and advises watching for phishing aimed at exposed administrator emails.

known.text: Microsoft says unauthorized parties read tenant-level metadata through a flaw in the Entra Connect Health API.
It says the flaw was introduced Jul 23 and discovered Nov 9.
It says a server-side fix went live Nov 19 and no customer update is needed.
It says it notified affected organizations on Nov 20.
It says the exposed data included administrator and technical-contact emails and tenant configuration metadata.
It says no passwords, tokens or valid keys were exposed (Microsoft's statement only).

not_known.text: Whether the exposed emails have been used in phishing.
Whether Microsoft's statement that no passwords, tokens or keys were exposed holds up.
